intro: Fine-tuning can change a linear layer through two small matrices while retaining its original weights. Trace the base prediction and low-rank update separately.
task: Implement a LoRA forward pass using supplied base weights, bias and adapter matrices. Scale the adapter update by alpha divided by its rank.
signature: lora_linear(x, weight, bias, a, b, alpha=1.0)
requirements: x has shape (..., in_features) with every dimension positive. weight is (out_features, in_features), bias is (out_features,), a is (rank, in_features), b is (out_features, rank); rank is positive.
Return x @ weight.T + bias + (x @ a.T @ b.T) * (alpha/rank), with shape (..., out_features).
alpha is a nonnegative real scalar. Use the supplied matrices without initialization or updates. This forward-only function has no training or frozen-parameter API.
Inputs must be real numeric values with finite magnitude at most 1e30. Leave inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Trace shapes
hints.body: First project input features into the rank-dimensional space with a, then back into output features with b.

hints.title: Check a zero adapter
hints.body: When b is all zeros, the full output must equal the base linear output, including its bias.

explanation: The adapter stores rank*(input_features+output_features) parameters. It can be smaller than a full weight update when the chosen rank is sufficiently low; this is not a universal saving for every shape.
The two multiplications compute the same output as adding (alpha/rank)*(b@a) to the base weight. A zero b initially leaves the base behavior unchanged.

The upstream class freezes its base layer and trains the adapter. This NumPy adaptation isolates the forward equation with supplied arrays; it does not simulate autograd or claim to verify training behavior.
